properties.abolition_note: Twenty-one-generation Mongour Tusi lineage seated at Laoyabao (Gaomiao) east of Ledu; formally abolished in August 1931 under the Qinghai Tusi abolition decree.
Tribal confederation around Chali Monastery and Jialuo; active autonomously until 1956.
Eastern Aba pastoral tribe; remained outside Sichuan Republican control until 1956.
Middle Aba Mocang Tuqianhu (Hua'erzong clan) and allied Ngawa tribes remained un-sinicised and autonomous until the 1956 Aba Democratic Reforms.
properties.name_zh: 阿坝莫尔盖部落联盟（中阿坝墨仓）

properties.abolition_note: Powerful Adi (formerly Abor) democratic village confederacies governed by Kebang assemblies across the middle and lower Siang (Yarlung-Dihang) basin; preserved Excluded Area and Kebang judicial autonomy past 1 January 1953.
properties.name_zh: 阿迪（珞巴阿波尔）凯邦部落联盟
properties.rank_title: Kebang Village Republics (Minyong, Padam, Galo, Pasi)

properties.abolition_note: Senior Adu Zhengzhangguansi seated in Puge; retained hereditary privileges until the 1956 Liangshan Democratic Reforms.
Butuo branch of the Adu Nuosu chieftaincy; active until 1956 Democratic Reforms.

Independent Hruso (Aka) chieftaincies (Jamiri, Thrizino/Buragaon, Bana) collecting posa blackmail/tribute from Assam borderland tracts and fiercely resisting external rule; remained self-governing in NEFA past 1 January 1953.

Autonomous western Khoshut Mongol banner outside the leagues, centred at Dingyuanying (Bayanhot). Last Jasaq Qinwang Darijaya (达理扎雅) led a peaceful uprising on 23 September 1949, ending hereditary Jasaq rule upon formation of the Alxa Khoshut Banner People's Government on 15 October 1949.
properties.name_zh: 阿拉善厄鲁特旗（阿拉善霍硕特旗）
properties.rank_title: Jasaq Khoshut Qinwang (扎萨克和硕亲王)

properties.abolition_note: CHGIS 1911 Yushusishizutusi polygon demarcating the historic Alike homeland around A'nye Maqen, Dawu (Maqin), and Gande; after the Alike clan migrated north across the Yellow River into Tongde and Xinghai, this domain became the heartland of the Upper Ngolok confederation, incorporated into PRC administration following the August 1952 Guoluo Working Group.

Seven Uriankhai banners transferred from Kobdo to the Altay Administrator in 1906-1907 and split along the Altai ridge during the 1912-1914 Outer Mongolian conflicts. The south-western banners entered Xinjiang's Ashan Circuit in 1919 under Chenghua/Fuyun administration while retaining tribal banner headmen until eroded by 1938-1944 Kazakh/Three Districts upheavals.
properties.name_zh: 阿尔泰乌梁海诸旗（阿山/阿勒泰部分）

properties.abolition_note: Tongtian River Baihu of the Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes; dissolved on 25 December 1951.
Abolished in August 1915 and combined with Duyang Tusi to form Du'an County (都安县).

Powerful Yellow River Tibetan qianhu domain at Angla (Jainca) ruled by Qianhu Wangchen (Xiangqian / Nangra); resisted early PRC integration in 1950-1952 until Xi Zhongxun's united-front negotiations brought Xiangqian to submit on 11 July 1952, followed by Jainca County formation in 1953.
properties.rank_title: Hereditary Tibetan Qianhu (昂拉千户项谦)

properties.abolition_note: Abolished in April 1928 and merged into Leiping County (雷平县).
Dense terraced-rice civilisation of the Apatani plateau governed by hereditary buliang village councillors; remained self-governing under NEFA Frontier Tract indirect oversight past 1 January 1953.
properties.name_zh: 阿帕塔尼（济罗盆地）部落联盟

properties.abolition_note: North-western Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes Baihu in Zhiduo; dissolved on 25 December 1951.
Tibetan frontier Tuqianzong controlling the Yunnan-Tibet-Sichuan tea trail at Atunzi; coexisted with the 1932 Deqin shezhiju until 1956-1957 Diqing democratic reform.
Upper Tongtian pastoral Baihu of the Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes in Zhiduo; dissolved on 25 December 1951.
Yin Changheng proclaimed gaituguiliu in 1912 to form Danba County, triggering the Three Tusis Rebellion; hereditary Badi lords retained de facto autonomy until the 1955-1956 Democratic Reforms.
Hereditary Yi Tubaihu along the Yuexi-Ganluo frontier; active until the 1955-1956 Liangshan Democratic Reforms.
Upper Tongtian Baihu of the Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes in Zhiduo; dissolved on 25 December 1951.
Target of Zhao Erfeng's 1911 reform and central to the 1930-1932 Beri-Dargye conflict; Beri chieftains persisted until 1956.
Retained Qing Zhangguansi (Zhou/Zhao clan) at Qiantao Qilongzhai south of Qingyan in Guizhu County; abolished during 1929-1935 Republican reorganisation.
Abolished in August 1915 and merged into Longshan County (隆山县).
Northern Baiyu metalworking and monastic enclave along the Jinsha east bank; retained autonomous headmen until 1956.
Highland Zengke pastoral tribes between Baiyu and Ganzi Mazur; self-governed until 1956.
Formerly Dege southern estates; converted to Baiyu County in 1909, yet local hereditary chieftains and Palyul monastery authorities governed de facto until 1956.
Acephaelous Bangni (Western Nyishi) longhouse clans along the upper Kameng (Pakke and Papu) rivers; remained unadministered tribal territory in NEFA past 1 January 1953.
properties.name_en: Bangni (Western Nyishi) Tribes of East Kameng

properties.abolition_note: Autonomous Awa Seventeen Kings federation under Banhong King Hu Yushan; integrated into Cangyuan democratic reform by 1956.

Allied with Banhong in the 1934 anti-British resistance; assigned across the 1941 Iselin Line, petitioned Beijing in late 1953, and remained autonomous under tribal elders past 1956 (retroceded 1960-1961).

Core Yushu plateau Baihu encompassing Gyegu (Jyekundo) and Baitang; later consolidated with Zhawu in Republican Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes lists while demarcated independently in CHGIS 1911; dissolved on 25 December 1951.

Founding monastic seat of the Barom Kagyu sub-school and its surrounding Nagchu-south pastoral estates; subordinated administratively to Nagchu/Horchi after 1916 yet retained estate autonomy until 1951.

Self-governing armed Miao highland village cluster above Bingmei (Congjiang) governed by customary zhailao and tree-worship elders outside county baojia and Republican taxation; remained autonomous beyond 1953.
properties.name_zh: 从江岜沙苗寨自治聚落

properties.abolition_note: Converted into Ba'an Prefecture by Zhao Erfeng in 1906, yet Batang gentry, monastery stewards, and former tusi networks exercised parallel de facto power through 1953 (reformed 1956).
Converted de jure into Danba County in 1912 under Yin Changheng, yet Bawang chieftains held local authority until the 1955-1956 reforms.
Remote Qiang headmen along the Qingpian valley retained customary self-rule after 1936 Republican baojia demarcation until the 1956 Democratic Reforms.
Hereditary Tibetan ferry-garrison Tuqianzong guarding the upper Jinsha (Yangtze) crossing into Batang and Derge; abolished 1956.

One of the Qing Ili Four Camps garrisoned in the Bortala River valley. Retained military-banner organisation under the Ili Defence Commissioner after 1912 (even after Bole County was carved out in 1920) until Sheng Shicai formally abolished all Ili banner camps (feiying gaixian) in January-February 1938 and established Wenquan Shezhiju.
properties.rank_title: Ili General Chahar Banner Camp (Left & Right Wing Zongguan)

properties.abolition_note: Western Yunlong mountain-pass Tubazong governing Lisu-Bai communities along the Nujiang divide until 1950.

Qinghai's sole monastic Lama Banner among the Twenty-Nine Banners, headed by the incarnate Shartsang Garbu / Chagan Nomun Khan (夏茸尕布活佛). Preserved de facto monastic-banner authority through the Republican era and past 1 January 1953 until dissolved with Hainan Tibetan Autonomous Region formation (December 1953) and 1958 democratic reforms.
properties.name_en: Chagan Nomun Khan Lama Banner (White Lama Banner)
properties.name_zh: 察汗诺们罕旗（白佛喇嘛旗）
properties.rank_title: Jasaq Lama / Chagan Nomun Khan (扎萨克喇嘛/夏茸尕布活佛)

properties.abolition_note: Major Kham Gelug principality governed by the Phagpalha Hutuktu around Jampaling Monastery; fell under Lhasa's Chamdo Governor (Doji) following the 1918 Kham Truce yet preserved extensive monastic estates until the Battle of Chamdo in October 1950.
properties.name_zh: 昌都帕巴拉呼图克图领地

properties.abolition_note: Autonomous Kongpo estate and hereditary local chieftainships centred along the lower Nyang River (Nyingchi and Buchu), maintaining distinct customs and tax exemptions under Lhasa past 1 January 1953 until 1959.

Nomadic yak-and-sheep pastoral tribes across the western Changtang basin of Gegyai, paying salt-and-butter tribute while retaining internal goba customary rule; active past 1 January 1953 until 1959 reforms.

Changpa pastoral tribes of the Taro Tso and Zhari Namtso basins (Gomo and Coqen), administered through hereditary nomadic elders under loose Lhasa/Tashilhunpo tax obligations; active on 1 January 1953 until 1959.

Semi-nomadic Changpa pastoral confederation of the Pangong and Rutog basins organised under hereditary tribal gobas and the Rutog Dzong; active on 1 January 1953 until Ngari pastoral democratic reforms in 1959.

Large autonomous Changpa tribal confederation of Gertse (Lumaringbo and Sertok) in the central-western Changtang lake belt; maintained nomadic self-governance past 1 January 1953 until the 1959 democratic reforms.
properties.rank_title: Hereditary Tribal Chiefs (sGer-rtse Goba / 天湖部)

properties.abolition_note: Pastoral tribes around Tangra Yumco and Nyima lake basins, historically linked to Bonpo and Changtang salt-caravan lineages; remained autonomous under local gobas past 1 January 1953 until 1959.
Nomadic tribes of Xainza (Zhocha and Doima sections) inhabiting the Kyaring Tso and Siling Co southern lake belt; active past 1 January 1953 until Nagqu democratic reforms in 1959.
Sovereign Sipsongpanna Xuanweishi (Zhaopianling Dao Chengen, Dao Dongliang, Dao Shixun); formally superseded on 23 January 1953 by the Xishuangbanna Dai Autonomous Region (active on 1 January 1953).
Hereditary Tusi house descended from Ming-invested commander Chen Ziming along the Beichuan-Datong valley north of Xining; abolished in August 1931 under the Qinghai Tusi abolition decree.

Major northern Yushu chieftaincy (aligned with Zhujie / Zhenqin in Republican Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes); despite Chengduo County establishment (1938), tribal Baihu authority persisted until 25 December 1951.
Created in 1776 after the Jinchuan Wars; hereditary military-agricultural chieftains governed locally until 1936.

Distinct CHGIS 1911 Yushu Si polygon along the lower Ziqu / Nyagla gorge; in the Republican Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes register it became affiliated with the Laxiu / Nangchen cluster and was dissolved on 25 December 1951.
Converted into Dengke Prefecture in 1909, but local Chunke and Dzogchen monastic-hereditary estates continued operating de facto until 1956.
Western Zaduo Baihu of the Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes on the Tangut-Tibet divide; dissolved on 25 December 1951.

One of two Choros Oirat banners in Qinghai (Right Wing League), centred on Quanji north of Qinghai Lake; retained banner status past 1 January 1953 until Haibei Tibetan Autonomous Region formation (December 1953).
properties.name_en: Choros North Middle Banner (Shuixia Beizi Banner)
properties.name_zh: 绰罗斯北中旗（水峡贝子旗）
properties.rank_title: Jasaq Gushan Beizi (扎萨克固山贝子)

properties.abolition_note: Senior Choros banner of Qinghai (Right Wing League), centred on Qabqa south-east of Qinghai Lake; retained banner status alongside Gonghe County (1929) past 1 January 1953 until Hainan Tibetan Autonomous Region formation (December 1953).
properties.name_en: Choros South Right Head Banner (Erlik Beile Banner)
properties.name_zh: 绰罗斯南右翼头旗（尔里克贝勒旗）
properties.rank_title: Jasaq Duoluo Beile (扎萨克多罗贝勒)

properties.abolition_note: Li clan Tuzhaizhang of southwestern Jinping in the Fifteen Mengs network; abolished 1953.
Independent Nuosu (Black Yi) clan confederation unadministered by Qing or Republican magistrates; integrated during the 1955-1957 Liangshan Democratic Reforms.
properties.name_zh: 大凉山诺苏黑彝自治核心区

properties.abolition_note: Eight Khoshut Mongol banners settled in the Damzhung valley in the 17th-18th centuries and placed under the Qing Amban in Lhasa until 1912; retained internal banner headmen and cavalry duties under Lhasa past 1 January 1953 until 1959.
properties.name_zh: 当雄八旗（达木蒙古八旗）
properties.rank_title: Hereditary Mongol Banner Confederation (达木八旗)

properties.abolition_note: Split from Geshizha following 1912 gaituguiliu; Dandong chieftains exercised autonomous control over the high alpine valley until 1956.
Fourth of the central Gyalrong Four Tusis; endured intact until 1956 Democratic Reforms.
After 1911 formal Daofu county establishment, Gaka clan chiefs controlled the upper Gaka-Songlinkou pastures until 1956.

Group of Drukpa Kagyu monastic estates around Mount Kailash (Darchen, Dirapuk, Zuthulpuk, Choku) granted to Bhutan in the 17th century and administered by a Bhutanese dzongpon representative; remained active on 1 January 1953 until absorbed by Ngari local authorities in the late 1950s.
properties.name_zh: 塔尔钦不丹飞地（冈仁波齐）
properties.rank_title: Drukpa Kagyu Monastic Estate (Under Bhutanese Lho-brug Representative)

properties.abolition_note: Bijie Datun Tusi Manor (Yu clan, descended from She Yi sub-chieftainship); Yu Dafu expanded the fortified manor compound in 1929 outside nominal county taxation until land reform confiscation in 1950.

Self-governing Yao mountain confederation ruled under customary shipai (石牌) stone-tablet covenants throughout the Republican era; formally integrated via the Dayao Shan Unity Pact (大瑶山团结公约) of 28 August 1951 and reorganised as the Dayao Shan Yao Autonomous Region (county level) on 28 May 1952.
properties.name_en: Dayao Shan Yao Autonomous Region (Shipai Polity)

properties.abolition_note: Abolished by Zhao Erfeng in 1909; restored de facto in 1918 following Tibetan-Sichuan armistices, with King Ngawang Jampel Rinchen and regent Xialideng reigning until 1956 Democratic Reforms.
Duan clan frontier Tuqianzong guarding Pianma-Gulang-Kangfang passes on the Gaoligongshan crest; abolished 1956.
Configured as Dengke County seat in 1909, yet hereditary tribal headmen held de facto sway east of the Jinsha until 1956.
Set up as Derong Weiyuan in 1908, while local tribal headmen controlled the lower Dingqu canyon until the 1956 Democratic Reforms.
Central Yushu Baihu unit (associated with Buqing / Laxiu pastures in Republican registers); dissolved on 25 December 1951.

Upper and Lower Tewo Tibetan canyon tribes nominally subordinate to Chone Yang Tusi and Xigu/Zhuoni Shezhiju (1937), yet exercising de facto local tribal autonomy through the Republican period and past 1 January 1953 until Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Region formation (October 1953) and 1958 reforms.
properties.rank_title: Tribal Headmen & Chiliarchs (迭部头人/千百户)

properties.abolition_note: Taraon (Digaru) Mishmi clans along the Digaru and middle Lohit valleys (Tezu, Hayuliang, Chaglagam); retained customary clan organisation and trans-border trade past 1 January 1953.
properties.name_zh: 达让（迪加鲁）米什米部落

properties.abolition_note: Abolished under early Republican gaituguiliu in 1912-1913 and merged into Nama County (那马县, later Mashan).
Retained Qing Zhangguansi (Luo clan Buyei) in Yongning/Guanling recorded in the 1929 Ministry of Interior native-office survey; dissolved during Guizhou provincial Tusi clearance (1929-1935).

Southern Monyul corridor (Dirang Dzong and Thembang Monpa villages) paying khral tax to Tsona/Lhasa through Tawang officials despite intermittent British NEFA patrols after 1938; brought under direct Indian NEFA Kameng Frontier Division administration in 1951.
properties.rank_title: Tibetan-Tributary Monpa Dzong & Tsorgon Councils (Dirang Dzong)

properties.abolition_note: Southern Nangchen sub-tribe along the Mekong-Kham frontier (listed in CHGIS 1911 under Yushusishizutusi and consolidated under Nangchen Qianhu in the Republican Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes); dissolved on 25 December 1951.
Converted into Baoxing County in 1928 under Sichuan warlord administration.
properties.name_zh: 董卜韩胡宣慰司（穆坪宣慰司）

properties.abolition_note: Designated for abolition in 1911; local Tibetan headmen persisted autonomously through Republican rule until 1955-1956.
Nominally converted in 1911; Dongkor monastery and chieftains ruled autonomously until 1956.
Southern Gejiu-Jianshui Yi/Hani Tuwaiwei and Tushe posts adjacent to Nalou; dismantled 1950.
properties.name_zh: 阿土-斗岩-六呼掌寨土外委

properties.abolition_note: Hereditary incarnate lama domain (Drayab Kyabgon / Hutuktu) holding administrative and judicial authority in southern Chamdo; retained monastic self-rule under Lhasa's eastern governor after 1918 until October 1950.
properties.rank_title: Hutuktu Monastic Principality (Brag-g.yab / 察雅活佛)

properties.abolition_note: Seat of the Drigung Kagyu lineage in upper Maizhokunggar, retaining tax-exempt monastic estates, dzong-equivalent jurisdiction, and sub-monasteries past 1 January 1953 until 1959.
Abolished in 1916 and merged into Zhenjie County (镇结县).
Abolished in 1917 and combined into Xiangdu County (向都县).
Agro-pastoral Amdo Tibetan tribes (Duxiu and Guomi) occupying the Chabcha / Gonghe basin between Qinghai Lake and the Yellow River gorge; retained local headmen until 1952.
properties.name_en: Duxiu & Guomi Tibetan Tribes of Gonghe
properties.rank_title: Tibetan Tribal Baihu & Headmen (都秀/果密百户)

properties.abolition_note: Abolished in August 1915 and merged with Anding Tusi into Du'an County (都安县).
Highland Ailao Yi Tumu / Tubazong headmanship along the Shuangbai-Xinping borderland; dissolved 1950.

Autonomous Torghut Mongol special banner along the lower Ruo Shui (Ejina River) and Juyan Oasis north of the Hexi Corridor. Last Jasaq Beile Tawanjab (塔旺嘉布) declared a peaceful uprising on 27 September 1949, terminating hereditary Jasaq governance.
properties.rank_title: Jasaq Duoluo Beile (扎萨克多罗贝勒)

properties.abolition_note: Abolished in 1913 under Guangxi administrative reorganisation and incorporated into Enyang County (恩阳县, later Tiandong).

All formal Hubei Tusi (Rongmei, Shinan, Tangya, Sanmao, Laifeng, Zhongjian) were abolished de jure in 1735 (Yongzheng 13); however, former tusi lineage strongmen and hereditary tumu/tuqianzong households in remote Xianfeng, Laifeng, Xuan'en, and Hefeng uplands retained local militia and corvee power (disrupted 1928-1935 by the Xiang-Exi Soviet) until 1950 PRC land reform.
properties.name_en: Southwestern Hubei Tujia Tumu & Tuqianzong Remnants
properties.name_zh: 鄂西土家族土目・土千总遗存区

properties.abolition_note: One of the Five Tun of Maogong; hereditary Tushoubei and Lijia administration lasted until the 1936 county consolidation.
Zhuang and Miao-Yao frontier Tumu headmanships bridging Funing and Tianpeng-Vietnam border passes; ended in 1950.
properties.name_zh: 富宁（富州）侬氏-剥隘土目

properties.abolition_note: Hereditary Hehuang Tusi family stationed at Gandu on the northern bank of the Yellow River opposite Xunhua; abolished in August 1931 under the Qinghai Tusi abolition decree.
One of the Lifan Five Tun; Gyalrong hereditary Tun officials remained active until Sichuan county reform in 1936.

Pre-eminent Huanhai (Koknor North Shore) Tibetan tribal confederation led by the Gangca Qianhu, who asserted pastoral dominance over former Khoshut Left Wing Head Banner pastures north of Qinghai Lake until integrated in 1952-1953.

Retained hereditary Dai/Achang Tusi authority alongside Republican administrative deputies and 1930s shezhiju (preparatory bureaus); formally abolished during Dehong's 1955 Peaceful Consultation Land Reform.
Eastern Yushu border Baihu between Gyegu and Derge across the Jinsha River; dissolved on 25 December 1951.
Major western Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes confederation (Upper, Middle, and Lower Gerji) straddling the Dangqu and upper Zaqu divide; dissolved on 25 December 1951.
properties.name_zh: 上中下格尔吉三司百户

properties.abolition_note: Hereditary Han clan Xuanfusi (last Xuanfushi Han Futing); abolished with establishment of Gengma Autonomous County in 1955.
Abolished de jure in 1912 with Danba County creation; Geshizha Zongguan remained active de facto through the Republican era until 1956.
Resisted Zhao Erfeng and Republican Xikang levies repeatedly; the Gonggaling monastery-chieftain confederation maintained de facto autonomy until 1956.
Nu-Drung clan headmanships across Changputong, Bingzhongluo, and Dulongjiang; linked to Yezhi/Weixi and 1932 Gongshan shezhiju until 1956.

Traditional Gonjo Tuqianhu chieftaincy west of the Jinsha River (adjacent to the San'yan valley); integrated into Lhasa's eastern frontier zone in 1918 while retaining clan chieftaincy authority until October 1950.
Ji clan Mosuo-Naxi Anfusi on the Yanyuan-Mianning-Muli border; maintained full tusi rule until 1956.
Retained Qing Zheng-Zhangguansi (Yang clan) in Kaiyang recorded in the 1929 Ministry of Interior native-office survey; hereditary title dissolved during Guizhou provincial Tusi clearance (1929-1935).
Ancient Zhuang Nong clan chieftaincy of Guangnan; formal office ended in early Republican county reforms while Nong lineage landlord-headman dominance survived until 1950.
Abolished in August 1916 and merged with Siling Tuzhou to form Sile County (思乐县). Distinct from Sizhou Prefecture in Guizhou.
Lang clan hereditary tusi of northern Yanyuan (Changbai / Wali); continued functioning until 1956 Democratic Reforms.
properties.name_zh: 古柏树巡城兵马司（长柏）

properties.abolition_note: Northern Tongtian River Baihu of the Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes; dissolved on 25 December 1951.
Abolished in August 1915 and merged with Guohua Tuzhou and Jiucheng Tusi to form Guode County (果德县, modern Pingguo).
Hexi Corridor Tibetan-Mongol frontier Tusi family at Dashagou in Gulang guarding the Wushaoling-Dajing passes; hereditary Tusi fiscal and judicial privileges were abolished in 1928.
properties.rank_title: Hereditary Tribal Tusi (古浪大沙沟土司)

properties.abolition_note: Abolished in August 1915 and united with Baishan Tusi and Xinglong Tusi to establish Longshan County (隆山县, modern Mashan).
Retained Qing Zhangguansi under Longli County (Song clan collateral); abolished during Republican Tusi clearance (1929-1935).
Abolished in August 1915 and merged with Guide Tuzhou and Jiucheng Tusi to form Guode County (果德县).

Middle and Lower Ngolok tribal confederations (Ashigong, Kangsar, Kanggan, and Banma) spanning Darlag, Jiuzhi, and the Banma forested valleys along the Qinghai-Sichuan divide; maintained fierce independence until the August 1952 Guoluo Working Group reached Jimai and Chalong Monastery, preceding the 1 January 1954 Guoluo Tibetan Autonomous Region.
properties.name_en: Lower Ngolok (Golok) Tribes (Ashigong, Kangsar, Kanggan & Banma)
properties.name_zh: 下果洛诸部（阿什羌、康赛、康干、班玛）
properties.rank_title: Ngolok Chiefdoms (Zong Qianhu / Baihu 头人)

properties.abolition_note: Autonomous Upper Ngolok pastoral confederation south of the Yellow River bend around A'nye Maqen, resisting Ma Bufang's expeditions through the Republican era; entered peaceful negotiations upon arrival of the Northwest Military-Administrative Committee Guoluo Working Group in August 1952, leading to the Guoluo Tibetan Autonomous Region on 1 January 1954.
properties.name_zh: 上果洛诸部（玛沁-甘德-昂欠本）
properties.rank_title: Hereditary Ngolok Tribal Headmen & Chiliarchs (千百户/昂欠本)

properties.abolition_note: Trans-Himalayan frontier valleys of Gyirong and Nyalam-Dram governed by local headmen, Brag-dkar rta-so monastic estates, and special Lhasa-Nepal treaty trade officials (until the 1956 Sino-Nepalese treaty); active past 1 January 1953.
properties.name_zh: 吉隆—聂拉木边境寺庙领地
properties.rank_title: Joint Frontier Monastic & Dzong Trade Jurisdiction

properties.abolition_note: Distinct CHGIS 1911 Si unit along the Tongtian-Zhaqu divide (affiliated with the Zhawu / Gyairong group in Republican Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes registers); dissolved on 25 December 1951.
Salar hereditary chieftaincy centred on Jishi (Xunhua); abolished in August 1931 under the Qinghai Provincial Government Tusi abolition decree.
properties.name_zh: 循化韩土司（撒拉土千户/积石）
properties.rank_title: Tu Qianhu / Tusi (撒拉族土千户)

properties.abolition_note: An clan hereditary Zhangguansi along the eastern Anning valley around Qionghai; retained status until 1955-1956.
Aligned with Su Yonghe's Heishui coalition; integrated into Lu'erhua (Heishui) County after the 1952 campaign.
Autonomous Heishui chieftaincy under Su Yonghe (Duoji Basang); defeated and abolished following the July 1952 PLA Heishui campaign.
Eastern gateway tribes of Heishui along the lower Heishui River; subdued alongside Mawo in the 1952 campaign.
Western Heishui alpine valley polity bordering Hongyuan Shuajingsi and Somang; absorbed during the 1952 Heishui pacification.
Northern Heishui tribal group bordering Songpan Mao'ergai; brought under direct county administration in 1952.

Senior banner of the Four Henan Mongol Banners south of the Yellow River, ruled by the hereditary Khoshut Qinwang lineage (last female Qinwang Tashi Tsering / 扎西才让, acceded 1941). Recognised by Republican Mengzang Weiyuanhui and retained de facto autonomy past 1 January 1953 until the Henan Mongol Autonomous District was formed in October 1954.
properties.name_en: Henan Khoshut Front Head Banner (Henan Qinwang)
properties.name_zh: 和硕特前头旗（河南亲王旗）
properties.rank_title: Jasaq Duoluo Junwang / Henan Qinwang (扎萨克和硕亲王)

properties.abolition_note: One of the Four Henan Mongol Banners (along the Zeku-Henan pastures south of the Yellow River); retained hereditary Jasaq status under Republican Mengzang Weiyuanhui oversight past 1 January 1953 until Zeku County (1953-1954) and Henan Mongol Autonomous District organisation.
properties.name_en: Henan Khoshut South Right Middle Banner (Datsan Banner)
properties.name_zh: 和硕特南右翼中旗（达参旗）
properties.rank_title: Jasaq Yideng Taiji (扎萨克一等台吉)

properties.abolition_note: Fourth of the Henan Mongol Banners, stationed around Ragya Monastery on the Yellow River; retained banner autonomy alongside Tongde County (1935) until the Hainan Tibetan Autonomous Region (December 1953) and Henan reorganisation (1954).
properties.name_en: Khoshut South Left Middle Banner (Ragya Banner)
properties.name_zh: 和硕特南左翼中旗（拉加扎萨克旗）
properties.rank_title: Jasaq Yideng Taiji (扎萨克一等台吉)

properties.abolition_note: One of the Four Henan Mongol Banners south of the Yellow River; retained banner autonomy under Republican Mengzang Weiyuanhui recognition and transitional PRC administration past 1 January 1953 until incorporation into the Henan Mongol Autonomous District in October 1954.
properties.name_en: Henan Torghut South Front Banner (Torghut Banner)

Hereditary Naxi/Tibetan frontier Tuqianzong guarding the Qizong-Tacheng Jinsha crossing; abolished 1956.
Abolished in September 1916 and merged with Longying and Mingying Tuzhou into Longming County (龙茗县, modern Daxin).

Direct descendant of the Tibetan Imperial Yarlung dynasty enjoying hereditary royal immunity, judicial autonomy, and ritual precedence in Lhoka (Qusum); active past 1 January 1953 until the 1959 democratic reforms.
properties.rank_title: Hereditary Prince of the Yarlung Royal House (Lha-rgya-ri Khri-chen)

properties.abolition_note: Independent upper Zamtang (Shangzhai) tribal polity; remained autonomous until Rangtang County formation and 1956 reforms.
Jonang monastic and lay tribal confederation centred on Zhong Rangtang; operated outside county control until 1956.
Mianning valley hereditary Tubaihu; active until the 1955-1956 Democratic Reforms.

Autonomous monastic principality of Reting (founded 1056) and associated Phenpo-north monasteries; despite the 1947 Reting Conspiracy crisis against the 5th Reting Rinpoche, the monastic estates persisted through 1 January 1953 until 1959.

Autonomous Taglung Kagyu monastic polity centred at Riwoche Monastery along the Ziqu river; remained under dual monastic-noble governance after 1918 until PLA integration during the October 1950 Chamdo Campaign.
properties.rank_title: Taglung Kagyu Hierarchate (Ri-bo-che / 类乌齐呼图克图)

properties.abolition_note: High-Himalayan frontier gorge polity of Rongshar on the Nepal-Tibet border, enjoying customary border-pass trade autonomy and monastic estate exemptions; active on 1 January 1953 until 1959.

Theocratic-secular dual polity of Rongwo Monastery (Shartsang Rinpoche) and the hereditary Rongwo Nangsuo ruling the Twelve Rebgong Tribes. Tongren County was formally created in 1929, yet the monastery-nangsuo domain retained de facto tribal and fiscal autonomy past 1 January 1953 until Huangnan Tibetan Autonomous Region formation (December 1953) and 1958 democratic reforms.
properties.name_zh: 隆务寺政教领地（同仁囊索/夏日仓）
properties.rank_title: Gelugpa Monastic-Nangsuo Principality (Shartsang Lama & Rongwo Nangsuo)

properties.abolition_note: Hereditary Upper and Lower Baozuo chieftains controlled the strategic Songpan-Gannan corridor through 1953 until 1956.
Songpan frontier tribal polity of Baxi and Axi; governed autonomously until 1956 Democratic Reforms.
Central Zoige plateau tribe nominally attached to Songpan 72 Tribes; retained autonomous rule until 1956.
Northern Heihe pastoral clans bordering Gansu Maqu; autonomous until 1956.
Sichuan-side Langmusi and Jiangzha clans along the Gansu Luqu frontier; self-governed until 1956.
Autonomous northern Songpan-Ruoergai tribe adjoining Gansu Diebu; remained intact until 1956.
Pastoral tribe controlling the Baihe-Yellow River confluence at Tangke; active autonomously until 1956.
Northernmost Sichuan-side Tebo valley clans bordering Gansu Diebu; remained outside county rule until 1956.
Large pastoral tribe in western Ruoergai bordering Gansu Luqu and Maqu; governed independently until 1956.

Semi-autonomous hereditary Sakya hierarchate (Khon lineage) exercising independent judicial, fiscal, and estate authority across the Chongchu valley in Tsang; remained active past 1 January 1953 until the 1959 democratic reforms.
properties.name_zh: 萨迦法王领地（萨迦寺政权）
properties.rank_title: Hereditary Hierarch (Sa-skya Khri-dzin / 萨迦法王)

properties.abolition_note: Unique female tulku (Samding Dorje Phagmo) ecclesiastical domain governing the Yamdrok Tso littoral and southern Nagarzê estates; active on 1 January 1953 until 1959.
properties.name_zh: 桑丁寺（多吉帕姆）羊卓雍领地
properties.rank_title: Dorje Phagmo Incarnate Estate (bSam-sdings rDo-rje Phag-mo)

properties.abolition_note: North-western Nangchen pastoral Baihu of the Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes; retained de facto autonomy until Yushu Tibetan Autonomous Region formation on 25 December 1951.
Southern Drukpa Kagyu monastic seat and Tsari pilgrimage-corridor estate in eastern Lhünzê bordering Subansiri tribal country; active past 1 January 1953 until 1959.
properties.name_en: Sangngak Choling & Lower Tsari Monastic Domain
properties.name_zh: 三安曲林寺（下杂日）领地

properties.abolition_note: Pacified briefly by Zhao Erfeng in 1910, the fortified Sanyan patrilineal clans resumed fierce independence on the Baiyu-Batang border until 1956.
Northern Seda pastoral federation bordering Qinghai Banma; fully independent of Sichuan and Xikang magistrates until 1955-1956.
Southern Seda / Serba pastoral clans bordering Luhuo and Rangtang; persisted autonomously until 1956.
An clan hereditary Xuanfusi dominating the eastern Liangshan borderlands; maintained autonomy until 1956.
Hereditary upper Ngawa Tuqianhu bordering Golok; persisted autonomously until 1956.
Incorporated on paper into Zhanhua County in 1911, contested by Lhasa governors (1914-1932) and Xikang forces, with local Nyagrong headmen remaining de facto until 1956.
Abolished in 1918 and merged with Xiawang Tusi to form Silin County (思林县, modern Tiandong/Pingguo border).
Abolished in July 1928 and incorporated into Shangjin County (上金县, modern Longzhou).
Mountain valley Tun of Lifan; hereditary Tushoubei institutions survived until 1936.
Lisu-Nu headman domains administered sequentially under Shangpa Colonisation Office and the 1932 Fugong shezhiju; integrated 1955.

Distinct northern CHGIS 1911 Si unit (Upper and Lower Alakshuo along the southern Tongtian bank at Haxe); historically merged into the Republican Laxiu Baihu lineage while spatially separate from Chuilengduoer and Laerji; dissolved on 25 December 1951.
properties.name_zh: 上下阿拉克硕二司百户

properties.abolition_note: Abolished in 1927 and incorporated into Longzhou County (龙州县).
Abolished in 1917 and merged with Dukang and Xiangwu Tuzhou to form Xiangdu County (向都县, modern Tiandeng).
Hereditary Dai Tubazong of the Shangyun basin under Zhenbian/Lancang; ended in 1951 land reform.
Nominally folded into Daofu Weiyuan in 1911; tribal headmen remained active until 1956 Democratic Reforms.
Retained Qing Zhangguansi under Yongning Zhou (Guanling); native chieftaincy dissolved during the 1929-1935 Republican reorganisation.
Monastic estate complex of Shelkar Chosde in Tingri holding extensive tax-exempt serf villages along the Phung Chu (Arun) plateau corridor; active past 1 January 1953 until 1959.
properties.name_zh: 协格尔曲德寺领地（定日）

properties.abolition_note: Yu clan Zhangguansi abolished de jure in late 1911 under Zhao Erfeng and absorbed into Luding County by 1912 under last chieftain Yu Qilin.

Autonomous Sherdukpen tribal community of Rupa and Shergaon, maintaining hereditary Thong aristocratic and Chhao commoner village councils, seasonal winter migration to Doimara, and NEFA Excluded Area customary autonomy past 1 January 1953.
properties.name_zh: 舍杜克本（鲁帕—舍尔冈）部落
properties.rank_title: Autonomous Tribal Thong & Chhao Councils (Rupa / Shergaon)

properties.abolition_note: North-western Shiqu pastoral clans under Serxu Gelugpa monastery and lay chiefs remained autonomous until 1956.
Eastern Shiqu tribal polity adjoining Qinghai Dari and Ganzi Seda; exercised self-rule until 1956.
Placed nominally under Shiqu County in 1909; nomadic Zaquka tribes maintained self-rule until the 1956 reforms.
Reduced from Xuanweisi to hereditary non-civil Tutongpan in 1761; the Ma clan's residual office ended formally when Shizhu Sub-prefecture became Shizhu County in 1913.

Created as subordinated Yi tumu estates when Shuicheng Ting was carved out in 1732; the Pawa, Yingbei, Disu, and Duoni Yi tumu houses kept armed serf-manors and customary courts until PRC land reform in 1950-1951.
properties.name_zh: 水城彝族土目（扒瓦・婴北・以舍）

properties.abolition_note: Descendant branches of the Shuixi An clan (48-mu system) held hereditary tumu domains across Dading/Dafang, Zhijin, and Nayong (split into Nayong County in 1941) until 1950 PRC land reform.
properties.name_zh: 水西大方・纳雍彝族土目

properties.abolition_note: Abolished in August 1916 and merged with Guangxi Tu-Sizhou to form Sile County (思乐县, modern Ningming).

Hereditary Singpho (Jingpo) duwa chieftaincies along the Noa-Dihing and Buri-Dihing plains (Bordumsa, Diyun, Miao), kin to Upper Burma Hukawng Jingpo; retained customary duwa status in NEFA past 1 January 1953.
properties.name_zh: 景颇（辛波）博尔杜姆萨—苗地区土酋
properties.rank_title: Hereditary Singpho Duwa / Gam Chiefs (Bordumsa / Miao)

properties.abolition_note: Retained Red River Jiangwai Zhangguansi/Tushe rule into the Republican Mengzi Circuit; integrated under Honghe County and Hani autonomous governance in 1950-1953.
One of the Four Gyalrong Tusis around Ma'erkang; remained autonomous until the 1956 reforms.
Wang clan hereditary Tuqianhu controlling Dadu River crossings at Anshunchang; formally abolished by the 24th Army in 1928.
South-western Songpan tribal group above Zhenjiangguan; preserved autonomy until 1956.
Senior Tuqianhu among the Songpan 72 Tribes along the Gonggangling-Huangshengguan corridor; active until 1956.
Western Songpan tribal unit among the 72 Tribes between Jin'an and Mao'ergai; autonomous until 1956.
Autonomous Songpan tribe along the upper Heishui-Minjiang watershed; preserved tribal rule until 1956.
Hereditary Tubaihu of northern Songpan; remained active until 1956 Aba reforms.
Kagyü monastic-affiliated Baihu of the Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes bordering Chamdo and Derge; retained de facto autonomy until 25 December 1951.
Northernmost of the Five Tun of Maogong; Tushoubei hereditary command operated alongside county magistrates until 1936.
South-western Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes Baihu along the upper Ziqu and Jiequ rivers; exempted in practice from the 1931 Qinghai Tusi abolition decree and dissolved on 25 December 1951.

Remote Puroik (Sulung) highland clans inhabiting the upper Kurung Kumey and Chayangtajo-north forests; largely uncontacted by colonial or early post-1947 NEFA administration until the late 1950s (active past 1 January 1953).

Seven-clan Yugur (Sariq Uyghur / Huangfan) nomadic confederation along the northern Qilian piedmont under hereditary Grand Headmen (大头目) and Qianhu; retained traditional tribal governance past 1 January 1953 until formal naming of the Yugur nationality (1953) and creation of the Sunan Yugur Autonomous District in February 1954.
properties.rank_title: Grand Headman & Chiliarch (七族黄番总管/大头目)

properties.abolition_note: Leading Gyalrong Xuanweisi; maintained full hereditary authority until Aba Democratic Reforms in 1956.
Jiang clan hereditary Tuqianhu (led in late Republic by female tusi Jiang Qiaobao); active until 1955-1956.

Independent Tagin clans of the upper Subansiri (Mara, Nacho, Taliha, Daporijo); fierce resistance to external penetration continued into the early 1950s (including the 1953 Achingmori incident), remaining de facto autonomous on 1 January 1953.
Placed under Taining Weiyuan in 1911, yet monastic-chieftaincy estates around Huiyuan Monastery persisted de facto until 1956.
Abolished in April 1928 and merged with Anping Tuzhou and Xialei Tusi to form Leiping County (雷平县, modern Daxin).

Ismaili Pamiri (Sarikoli & Wakhi) Tajik community centred on Tashkurgan stone fortress and the Taghdumbash Pamir; retained hereditary begs, border-militia service, and local customs until 1950 PLA arrival (and 1954 autonomous county creation).
properties.name_zh: 色勒库尔（塔什库尔干）塔吉克部落
properties.rank_title: Hereditary Tajik Beg & Aksakal Leadership (Sarikol / Puli)

properties.abolition_note: Cross-border monastic polity north of the Bailong River headwaters (Sertri Monastery on the Gannan side, paired with Kirti on the Zoige side); maintained autonomous monastic and tribal governance through the Republican era and past 1 January 1953 until Gannan Tibetan Autonomous Region integration (October 1953) and the 1958 Gannan reforms.
properties.name_zh: 达仓郎木寺政教领地（赛赤寺）

properties.abolition_note: Southernmost Tibetan-tributary Monpa estate centred on Talung Dzong (Kalaktang, Morshing, Domkho, Sanglem) near the Bhutanese-Assam duars; administered locally with monastic ties to Tawang until NEFA integration in 1951.
properties.name_zh: 达隆宗（卡拉克塘）门巴领地

properties.abolition_note: Cluster of Tangsa (Naga-affiliated) sub-tribes straddling the Patkai Range and Pangsau Pass into northern Myanmar; preserved customary clan governance under NEFA Tirap Frontier Tract past 1 January 1953.
properties.name_en: Tangsa (Tase) Chieftaincies of the Patkai Range
properties.rank_title: Autonomous Patkai Clan Confederacies (Tangsa / Lungchang / Mossang)

properties.abolition_note: Retained Qing Dong-Miao Zhangguansi (Shi clan) in Liping Prefecture; abolished during the 1929-1935 Guizhou Tusi clearance.

Ancient Tibetan-Qiang Zan clan Tusi of Taozhou holding hereditary military-colony lands north and east of Chone; absorbed into regular Lintan County administration during the 1928 Gansu provincial reform.
properties.rank_title: Hereditary Guard Tusi (洮州卫昝土司)

properties.abolition_note: Extensive quasi-sovereign monastic domain of the Panchen Lama's Tashilhunpo Labrang across Shigatse, Lhazê, Namling, and Xaitongmoin; after the 9th Panchen Lama's December 1923 flight, the Lhasa Kashag placed Labrang estates under direct fiscal receivership from 1924 to 1951 while preserving the estate cadastre, before full restoration under the 1951 Seventeen-Point Agreement and 1952 return of the 10th Panchen Lama (active on 1 January 1953 until 1959).
properties.name_zh: 扎什伦布寺（班禅拉章直属领地）
properties.rank_title: Autonomous Ecclesiastical Principality (Bla-brang / 班禅堪布会议厅)

properties.abolition_note: Pari (Huarui) Tibetan tribes (Duoshi, Songshan, Tiantang Monastery) along the Wushaoling and Datong corridors. Following the 1931-1932 abolition of Liancheng Lu Tusi overlordship and creation of the Tianzhu administrative district (1936), local tribal Qianhu/Baihu authority persisted until the Tianzhu Autonomous District was formed on 6 May 1950.
properties.name_zh: 天祝（华锐）藏族部落与寺院
properties.rank_title: Tribal Chiliarchs & Gelugpa Monasteries (千百户/天堂寺)

properties.abolition_note: Semi-autonomous western Tibetan viceregal administration centred on Gartok, governing Guge, Purang, and Gar under two Lhasa-appointed Garpöns with broad local fiscal and border-trade autonomy; active on 1 January 1953 until Ngari Prefecture reorganisation after 1954-1959.
properties.rank_title: Joint Viceroys of Ngari (Gar-dpon / 堆噶本)

properties.abolition_note: Bai/Naxi Luo clan lineage (descended from Lanzhou Tuzhou) holding hereditary chieftaincy over Tu'e and upper Lanping past 1953 until 1956 democratic reform.

Qinghai Left Wing League Torghut banner along the Daheba and Ziketan pastures of Xinghai; active alongside Xinghai Shezhiju (1943) past 1 January 1953 until Hainan Tibetan Autonomous Region formation (December 1953).
properties.name_zh: 土尔扈特南后旗（角昂扎萨克旗）
properties.rank_title: Jasaq Yideng Taiji (扎萨克一等台吉)

properties.abolition_note: Qinghai Right Wing League Torghut banner south-west of Qinghai Lake in Xinghai; retained Jasaq status past 1 January 1953 until incorporated into the Hainan Tibetan Autonomous Region (December 1953).
properties.name_en: Torghut South Middle Banner (Yongan / Danba Banner)
properties.name_zh: 土尔扈特南中旗（永安扎萨克旗）
properties.rank_title: Jasaq Yideng Taiji (扎萨克一等台吉)

properties.abolition_note: Torghut banner seated near Qagan Us (Dulan); retained Jasaq tribal authority alongside Dulan County (1930) past 1 January 1953 until replaced by Haixi Autonomous Region in January 1954.
properties.name_zh: 土尔扈特西旗（托里合扎萨克旗）
properties.rank_title: Jasaq Yideng Taiji (扎萨克一等台吉)

properties.abolition_note: While the Qing abolished the Turpan Jasagh banner administration during Xinjiang provincehood in 1884, Emin Khoja's descendants retained their hereditary Junwang title (elevated to Qinwang under Emin Khoja's descendant Yiming Khoja in 1913), the Lukchun palace, and substantial oasis land-and-serf estates through 1931 until the 1932-1933 Turpan uprising and the burning of the Lukchun palace in 1933.
properties.name_zh: 吐鲁番鲁克沁郡王（亲王）领地
properties.rank_title: Hereditary Duoluo Junwang / Qinwang (Emin Khoja Lineage)

properties.abolition_note: Upper Wangshidaike Tibetan tribes settled in the Daheba and Heka valleys of Xinghai (historically Torghut South Rear Banner pastures); exercised tribal autonomy until Hainan/Xinghai county establishment in 1952-1953.
properties.rank_title: Tibetan Qianhu / Baihu Confederation (上王什代克)

properties.abolition_note: Last of the Zuojiang Zhuang native subprefectures; abolished in August 1929 and converted into regular Wancheng County (万承县, modern Daxin), completing Guangxi formal county conversion prior to 1 January 1930.

Hereditary Wancho (Konyak-allied) paramount chieftaincies ruled by Wangham princes over Longding, Niausa, Wakka, and Pongchau; retained traditional morung and chieftaincy autonomy well past 1 January 1953.
properties.name_zh: 万乔（隆丁）世袭王公部落

properties.abolition_note: Jing clan Dai Tuzhou; Republican Changning County absorption began in 1932 while hereditary Jing Shaowen authority survived de facto until 1949.
Western Huangshui valley Tusi house among the Sixteen Xining Houses; abolished in August 1931 under the Qinghai Tusi abolition decree.
Nominally subsumed in 1906, yet the Chongxi chieftain lineage persisted as major powerbrokers across southern Litang and Yajiang until 1956.
Nominally affected by Litang 1906 gaituguiliu, yet Maoya pastoral chieftains continued exercising autonomous authority over the Maoya grasslands until 1956.
Listed under Litang 1906 gaituguiliu on paper; Washu Qudeng hereditary chiefs retained control of the northern Litang-Baiyu divide until 1956.
Unconquered by Zhao Erfeng; autonomous pastoral tribes of Seda remained outside county administration until Seda County was formed in 1955 and reformed in 1956.
properties.name_zh: 瓦述色他长官司（色达部落）

properties.abolition_note: Nominally placed under Daofu in 1911; nomadic Washu Yuke pastures stayed autonomous under clan chieftains until 1956.
Sichuan provincial reforms sought to abolish hereditary titles in 1936, but last Suo family chieftain Suo Guanying retained authority in Wenchuan until 1955.
Retained Red River Jiangwai Zhangguansi/Tushe rule into the Republican Mengzi Circuit; integrated under Honghe County and Hani autonomous governance in 1950-1953.
Zhang clan hereditary Zhangguansi in Dechang; survived under last chieftain Zhang Mingxi until 1956 Democratic Reforms.

Following Qing abolition of Wusa Tufu (1666) and Shuixi adjustments (1729), the An, Lu, and Long Yi Tumu lineages retained armed feudal manors across western Weining/Hezhang (led by Lu Zhenxiang and Long Yunqiao) until PLA bandit-suppression and land reform in 1950-1951.
properties.name_en: Weining Niupeng Yi Tumu (Eight Great Tumu)

properties.abolition_note: Yang Chunpu held the Wori Anfusi until his death; his widow Sun Yongzhen led a rebellion suppressed by PLA forces in 1951.
Highland Nasu Yi lineage-headmen (descended from Wuding Feng/Na houses) wielding de facto militia and estate control north of Luquan until 1950.
properties.name_en: Wuding-Luquan Na & Feng Clan Yi Tumu
properties.name_zh: 武定-禄劝那氏·凤氏彝族土目

properties.abolition_note: Cluster of contiguous Hani Tuzhaizhang villages across southern Yuanyang; abolished 1951.
Lower Aba Aqiang tribal polity along the Ake River; remained independent until 1956 Democratic Reforms.
Grouped under Zhanhua in 1911, yet southern Nyagrong clans resisted both Xikang and Tibetan levies and kept de facto autonomy until 1956.
Abolished in April 1928 and merged with Taiping and Anping Tuzhou into Leiping County (雷平县).
Lower Mengtun valley Tun under Lifan; hereditary Tun governance discontinued in 1936.
Converted into Dingxiang County in 1906, yet armed monastic and lay headmen around Sangpi Monastery governed autonomously until 1956.
Abolished in 1917 and combined into Xiangdu County (向都县).

Post-1797 Miaojiang tuntian military-native office system (Miao Tushoubei, Tuqianzong, Tubazong) administered by the Republican Tunwu Chu under Chen Quzhen across Yongsui, Fenghuang, Qianzhou, Baojing, and Guzhang; abolished following the 1937 Ge-tun uprising and 1937-1938 Hunan provincial fei-tun shengke decree.
properties.name_en: Western Hunan Miaojiang Tunzheng (Native Garrison Offices)
properties.name_zh: 湘西苗疆屯防（土守备・土千总制）

properties.abolition_note: Abolished in 1927 and incorporated into Pingxiang County (凭祥县) along the Sino-Vietnamese frontier.
Abolished in 1918 and merged with Shanglin Tuxian into Silin County (思林县).
Hereditary Dai Tuqianzong centred at Menglangba / Xiayun; displaced during 1951 Lancang agrarian transformation.
Formal deputy office attached to Langdai Ting in 1731, while Wen lineage tumu estate authority over Machang and Xibu villages persisted until Republican administrative clearance in 1929.
Retained Red River Jiangwai Zhangguansi/Tushe rule into the Republican Mengzi Circuit; integrated under Honghe County and Hani autonomous governance in 1950-1953.
Western Daliangshan Nuosu clan domains along the Sunshui valley between Xichang and Zhaojue; autonomous until 1956 reforms.

Baima and Amdo Tibetan mountain tribes (Gongba, Boyu, Fengdie, Bazang) along the Bailong gorge; formally placed under Xigu County in 1913 yet retaining de facto tribal headman structures past 1 January 1953 until Gannan integration and the Zhouqu Administrative Committee (1954).
properties.name_zh: 舟曲（西固）藏族土官部落
properties.rank_title: Native Headmen & Tribal Banners (西固番部头人)

properties.abolition_note: Autonomous Ximeng Wa headman confederation (Masan, Yuesong, Mengsuo); democratic transition completed 1956.
properties.name_zh: 卡瓦山区部落联盟（西盟）

properties.abolition_note: Native Tusi lineage of the Sixteen Xining Houses situated in southern Minhe (Bazhou and Gushan); abolished in August 1931 under the Qinghai Tusi abolition decree.
properties.name_zh: 辛家土司（民和巴州/碾伯）

properties.abolition_note: Mo clan native county abolished in April 1928 and reorganised as regular Xincheng County (忻城县).
Abolished in August 1915 and incorporated into Longshan County (隆山县).
Retained Qing Zhangguansi (Song clan) in Guiding County; hereditary native office dissolved during Guizhou Republican clearance (1929-1935).
Although Hekou County was formed in 1906-1911, local Tibetan Tubaihu along the Jianzishan-Xigolog plateau remained active de facto until 1956.
properties.name_zh: 雅江河口土百户（西俄洛）

properties.abolition_note: Hereditary frontier Tusi along the Yellow River basin of Guide; abolished in August 1931 under the Qinghai Provincial Government Tusi abolition decree.
Retained Qing Zhangguansi (Guo clan) in Longli County; hereditary office terminated during Guizhou provincial Tusi clearance (1929-1935).
Retained Qing Zhangguansi (Cai clan) under Xifeng/Kaiyang north of Guiyang; abolished during Guizhou provincial Tusi clearance (1929-1935).
Retained Qing Zhangguansi (Jin clan) under Pingyue Zhou (Fuquan); abolished during Guizhou provincial Tusi clearance (1929-1935).
Retained Qing Tujia Zhangguansi (Zhang clan) in Yanhe/Si'nan; dissolved during the 1929-1935 Guizhou Tusi clearance.
Eastern Awa highland Wa tribal confederation between Cangyuan and Shuangjiang; integrated during 1955 democratic reform.
Bai/Bu clan hereditary Tubaihu; endured until 1956.
A clan hereditary Mosuo Tubaihu north of Zuosuo; remained active until 1956 Democratic Reforms.
Ba clan hereditary Tuqianhu of eastern Yanyuan; active until the 1956 reforms.
La clan hereditary Tuqianhu southwest of Yanyuan county seat; survived intact until 1956.
Hereditary La clan Mosuo Tuqianhu on the eastern shore of Lugu Lake; retained full tusi authority until 1956 Democratic Reforms.
Uyghur/Semu-descended hereditary Tusi house of the Sixteen Xining Houses seated at Nianbo (Ledu); abolished in August 1931 under the Qinghai Tusi abolition decree.
Tongtian River Baihu of the Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes; dissolved on 25 December 1951.
Naxi/Tibetan Wang clan theocratic-military Tuqianzong on the upper Mekong; survived Weixi county conversion in 1913 until the 1956-1957 democratic reform.
Cao clan Tea Mountain Tuqianzong; merged under Xiangming/Zhenyue County in 1929 while Cao family lineage authority persisted until 1950.
properties.name_zh: 倚邦土把总（曹氏茶山土司）

properties.abolition_note: Separated from Batang as Sanyan/Yidun County in Republican planning, but pastoral clans and Chokpo Monastery held autonomous power until 1956.
Six Great Tea Mountains Tuqianzong (Wu clan); incorporated into Zhenyue County in 1929 while retaining local gentry-headman tax roles into early 1950s.
properties.name_zh: 易武土千总（古六大茶山）

properties.abolition_note: Prominent Mongol-descended Lu clan Tusi of Zhuanglang (Pingfan/Yongdeng), holding vast Datong River estates centred on Liancheng; formally abolished in 1931 under the Nationalist/Qinghai-Gansu anti-Tusi ordinances alongside adjacent Hehuang Tusis.
properties.rank_title: Hereditary Guard Commander Tusi (庄浪卫鲁土司)

properties.abolition_note: Provincial gaituguiliu decree issued in late 1927; Zhangguansi jurisdiction dissolved into Yishan County in 1928.
A clan Mosuo Tufu (Zongguan) at Lugu Lake; active on 1 January 1953 and abolished during the 1956 Ninglang democratic reform.
Large north-eastern Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes Baihu spanning the Bayan Har pass towards Maduo; dissolved on 25 December 1951.
Historically co-ruling Gao and Zhang Tusi clans of Beisheng/Yongbei; titular authority phased out in early Republican reforms while clan estates lingered until 1949.
properties.name_zh: 永胜高氏-章氏土州同遗系

properties.abolition_note: Provincial gaituguiliu decree issued in late 1927; deputy Zhangguansi office dismantled and incorporated into Yishan County in 1928.
Provincial gaituguiliu decree issued in late 1927; hereditary Zhangguansi authority dismantled and incorporated into Yishan County in 1928.
Na clan Dai-Yi hereditary Tushe lineage around the Yuanjiang valley; customary landlord/lineage power ended in 1950.
Autonomous Black Yi clans controlling the Xiaoxiangling and Puxiong high plateau between Yuexi and Xide; integrated in 1956.
North-western division of the Yushu Four Tribes spanning the Chumar headwaters and Kunlun Pass corridor; dissolved on 25 December 1951.
properties.name_en: Yushu Second Division (Yushu Er Si) Baihu
properties.name_zh: 玉树二司百户（可可西里）

properties.abolition_note: Central division of the Yushu Four Tribes between the Chumar and Tuotuo rivers; dissolved on 25 December 1951.
properties.name_en: Yushu Third Division (Yushu San Si) Baihu

properties.abolition_note: South-westernmost division of the Yushu Four Tribes along the Tuotuo, Dangqu, and Tanggula pass; dissolved on 25 December 1951.

properties.abolition_note: Abolished de jure during Zhao Erfeng's 1911 gaituguiliu, but hereditary Jia clan chieftain Jia Anren retained local control until his armed uprising was suppressed in 1951.
Lead garrison of the Lifan Five Tun; hereditary Tushoubei authority persisted through early Republican era until 1936.

Small Buddhist Meyor (Zakhring) borderland community inhabiting Walong, Dong, Kibithoo, and Kahao below Rima/Zayul along the upper Lohit corridor; maintained autonomous village governance past 1 January 1953.

properties.abolition_note: Retained hereditary Dai/Achang Tusi authority alongside Republican administrative deputies and 1930s shezhiju (preparatory bureaus); formally abolished during Dehong's 1955 Peaceful Consultation Land Reform.
Zhao Erfeng established Luhuo Tun in 1911, but the Hor Zhanggu chieftaincy exercised continuous de facto authority until 1956.
Eastern Danba / Xiaojinchuan confluence garrison; hereditary Tun chieftaincy ended in the 1936 provincial reorganisation.
Hereditary Tusi house of southern Ledu near Qutan Monastery (part of the Sixteen Xining Houses); abolished in August 1931 under the Qinghai Tusi abolition decree.
Major Yushu Twenty-Five Tribes chieftaincy centred on Xiwu along the Tongtian River; dissolved on 25 December 1951.

Retained hereditary Dai/Achang Tusi authority alongside Republican administrative deputies and 1930s shezhiju (preparatory bureaus); formally abolished during Dehong's 1955 Peaceful Consultation Land Reform.
Wang clan frontier Lahu-Dai Tuzhaizhang of the Lin'an Fifteen Mengs (Jinping County formed 1933); abolished in early 1950s border democratic reform.
Historical Dai-Lue Banna granary chieftaincy (ancestral seat of Zhao Cunxin); active into early 1950s under Jiangcheng frontier administration.

Formally converted to Zhenkang county administration in 1906-1907 following heirless succession disputes, yet cadet Dao clan Tumu and valley headmen exercised de facto feudal power across Yongkang and Zhenkang until 1950.
Abolished in 1916 and combined with Jie'an, Jielun, and Dujie native subprefectures to form Zhenjie County (镇结县, later Tiandeng).
Converted into Huairou/Zhanhua County in 1911; occupied by Lhasa troops 1914-1932 and recovered by Xikang in 1932, with indigenous Nyagrong chieftains active until 1956.
Retained Qing Zhangguansi (Xie clan) in Guizhu County south of Guiyang; title dissolved during Republican Tusi clearance (1929-1935).
Dual Tibetan monastic (Ganden Sumtseling) and hereditary Tuqianzong authority governing Zhongdian plateau pastures until the 1956-1957 Diqing democratic reform.
properties.name_zh: 中甸土千总（松赞林寺政教领地）

properties.abolition_note: Abolished in July 1916 and reorganised as Zhong County (忠县), shortly renamed Suilu County (绥渌县, modern Fusui).
Sichuan Gyalrong chieftaincy; survived intact through 1953 until formal abolition in 1956.

Hereditary Yang clan Amdo Tibetan chieftaincy governing 48 banners along the Tao River. Following the August 1937 Boyu Incident (murder of Yang Jiqing), Gansu Province decreed de jure gaituguiliu and established the Zhuoni Shezhiju in September 1937; however, Yang Fuxing retained de facto Tusi command until 11 September 1949, when he declared allegiance to the PRC and dissolved Tusi rule.
Remained intact throughout the Republic; Choschia chieftaincy peacefully transitioned during the 1955-1956 Aba reforms.
Subsumed nominally into Luhuo County in 1911-1914; Zhuwo chieftains retained autonomous rule until 1956 Democratic Reforms.
Nominally folded into Daofu Weiyuan in 1911; sub-tribal headmen retained de facto rule until the 1956 Ganzi reforms.
Hani-Yi mountain Tuzhaizhang in southern Yuanyang (Panzhihua-Aicun terraces) linked to the Fifteen Mengs; ended 1951.
Retained Red River Jiangwai Zhangguansi/Tushe rule into the Republican Mengzi Circuit; integrated under Honghe County and Hani autonomous governance in 1950-1953.
